transcript.text: Zanussi dishwasher keeps tripping the electrics, not every time though. Usually about 15 mins in. Model ZDT21006FA

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. The most common cause for trips occurring around 15 minutes into a cycle is a failing heater element that has developed an 'earth leak' (insulation breakdown), causing the RCD to trip when it tries to heat the water. Please stop using the appliance until a qualified engineer can inspect and repair it. Using it risks further tripping or electrical shock. To help the engineer diagnose this, please note: does the trip happen precisely as soon as the heating stage begins (usually 10-20 mins in), or at other points? Also, is there any visible damage to the power cable or plug?

It's usually 10-20 mins in on the 65C programme, and the quick cold rinse never trips it. I can't see any damage on the cable or plug. It's a shared kitchen circuit with the fridge on it too, so that's a bit worrying.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
The fact that the quick cold rinse never trips it, but the 65C programme does after about 10–20 minutes, suggests that the heating stage is triggering the fault. In a dishwasher like your Zanussi ZDT21006FA, this almost always points to the heater element developing an 'earth leak' (insulation breakdown) or, less commonly, a fault in the circulation pump wiring. Because this involves mains electricity and water, please do not attempt to open the machine yourself. You must leave it unplugged and have a qualified appliance engineer inspect it. They will need to test the heater element's resistance to earth to confirm if it needs replacing. The shared circuit with your fridge is likely just coincidental; RCDs trip on leakage faults regardless of other appliances on the same ring main, provided they are on the same protected circuit.
